memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of both knees.
Evidence: Patient reports bilateral knee pain worsening with stairs and prolonged standing, morning stiffness <30 minutes, occasional crepitus. Examination shows mild medial joint line tenderness, slight warmth, no effusion, full range of motion. Smoking status: never. Plan: weight‑bearing X‑ray of both knees, serum vitamin D level, start paracetamol 650 mg SOS, topical diclofenac gel BD, calcium‑vitamin D3 OD. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Paracetamol 650 mg oral SOS max 4 g/day; Diclofenac sodium 1% gel apply to affected knees twice daily; Calcium carbonate 500 mg with Vitamin D3 400 IU oral once daily. Dispense 30 days.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum 25‑hydroxy Vitamin D: 18 ng/mL (Reference 30‑100 ng/mL). Indicates vitamin D deficiency.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I've been having more pain in my right knee when walking to work, especially after night shifts. The gel helps a bit but I need something stronger.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2025-07-10 at 10:00 AM with Dr Suresh Menon for osteoarthritis follow‑up.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knees, moderate progression.
Evidence: Pain VAS 6/10, morning stiffness ~45 minutes, crepitus on movement, mild joint line tenderness, slight effusion of right knee. Smoking status: never. Plan: continue paracetamol SOS, increase diclofenac gel to TDS, add calcium‑vitamin D3 OD, repeat vitamin D level, arrange weight‑bearing X‑ray.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Paracetamol 650 mg oral SOS max 4 g/day; Diclofenac sodium 1% gel apply to affected knees three times daily; Calcium carbonate 500 mg with Vitamin D3 400 IU oral once daily. Dispense 30 days.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Weight‑bearing X‑ray both knees: Joint space narrowing medially grade 2, osteophytes at tibial and femoral margins, subchondral sclerosis. No acute fracture.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum 25‑hydroxy Vitamin D: 22 ng/mL (Reference 30‑100 ng/mL). Still insufficient; advise higher supplement.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Orthopaedic Surgery, Dr K. Rao, for evaluation of possible knee arthroplasty due to progressive osteoarthritis.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Orthopaedic review: Patient symptomatic, X‑ray shows moderate OA. Recommended trial of intra‑articular hyaluronic acid injection and physiotherapy before considering surgery.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knees, symptomatic despite medical therapy.
Evidence: Pain VAS 5/10, stiffness 30 min, mild effusion left knee, crepitus bilateral. Smoking status: never. Plan: administer hyaluronic acid injection as advised, continue paracetamol SOS, topical diclofenac TDS, calcium‑vitamin D3 OD, repeat vitamin D in 3 months, review in 6 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Paracetamol 650 mg oral SOS max 4 g/day; Diclofenac sodium 1% gel apply to affected knees three times daily; Calcium carbonate 500 mg with Vitamin D3 400 IU oral once daily. Dispense 30 days.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knees, improved after injection.
Evidence: Pain VAS 3/10, stiffness <15 minutes, no effusion, crepitus mild. Smoking status: never. Plan: continue current regimen, advise low‑impact exercise, repeat vitamin D level, review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Paracetamol 650 mg oral SOS max 4 g/day; Diclofenac sodium 1% gel apply to affected knees twice daily; Calcium carbonate 500 mg with Vitamin D3 400 IU oral once daily. Dispense 30 days.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment changed from 2026-04-20 to 2026-03-15 at 09:30 AM with Dr Suresh Menon for osteoarthritis review.
